sources.title: Tunica-Biloxi Tribe: General Profile
sources.note: Direct tribal history. Uses river trade, 1779 campaigns, early twentieth-century subsistence, 1919 cotton collapse and 1981 recognition. Does not adopt disputed Quizquiz identification, inconsistent 1694 mission date or broader Biloxi-contact conjecture.

sources.title: Jeffrey P. Brain: On the Tunica Trail, Chapter 2
sources.note: Direct scholarly archaeological booklet reproduced by Louisiana Anthology; original Louisiana Division of Archaeology digital-books listing links an unavailable original. Chapter quotes La Source 1699 and Gravier; farming division is attributed historical observation, not a timeless rule. Salt manufacture paragraph cites Swanton.

sources.title: Tunica-Biloxi Tribe: The Tunica Treasure, museum handbook
sources.note: Direct 16-page primary museum handbook, David Watt with tribal editors. Printed pages 3, 5, 7 and 9. No generalized NAGPRA legal claim or precise all-artifact count adopted.

sources.title: Bureau of Indian Affairs: Tunica-Biloxi acknowledgment evidence and specialist reports
sources.note: Direct 84-page government evidence packet. PDF pages 1 to 4 distinguish allied ancestral peoples and nineteenth-century amalgamation. PDF page 48, anthropology report printed page 20, describes 1938 delegation and its requests. Historical report is not a present-day membership census.

sources.title: Tunica-Biloxi Tribe: Conservation Lab
sources.note: Direct tribal account of 1989 possession, two refrigerated truck trailers, member training and 2011 CERC laboratory.

sources.title: John Barbry: Taluhchi Yoroni Woruhk’iti
sources.note: Direct tribal language-program account. Heading gives exact Tunica phrase and English translation. Body documents 2010 partnership, 2011 illustrated book and youth recordings, 2012 camps and 2014 program. No stale present-day speaker count repeated.

sources.title: Tunica-Biloxi Tribe: Textbook to Aid in Language Revitalization Efforts
sources.note: Official June 12, 2023 release, directly indexed full relevant text: spring 2023 textbook, Haas and Youchigant documentation, letter to Haas and community teaching.

sources.title: Chitimacha Tribe of Louisiana: Tribal History
sources.note: Direct tribal account, homeland, matrilineal clans documented in early twentieth century, 1706 to 1718 war, displacement, land struggles, 1916 trust and 1970/1971 constitution. Does not adopt comparative most-powerful, most-enslaved or only-tribe superlatives.

sources.title: Atchafalaya National Heritage Area: Chitimacha Indian Reservation
sources.note: Full indexed original heritage trail account, houses, water travel, subsistence and settlement. Does not use uncertain precise 500 CE settlement or contact population estimates.

sources.title: Chitimacha Tribe: Chitimacha Baskets
sources.note: Direct tribal account, rivercane, colors, dyes, elbow baskets and double-woven containers. Does not repeat changing number of weavers or universal watertightness.

sources.title: National Endowment for the Arts: Ada Thomas
sources.note: Direct 1983 National Heritage Fellow biography including first-person recollections. One-room school, grandmother and aunt, exclusion from local high schools, renewed basketry and continuous double weaving.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Ada Vilcan Thomas, Basket with Lid, 1989
sources.note: Direct collection entry 2022.428.2a,b, actual creation year 1989, rivercane and Alligator Entrails pattern.

sources.title: Chitimacha Tribe: Education
sources.note: Full indexed original read; direct page cache miss. Reproducible query site:chitimacha.gov "1932" "1934" school. Describes Carlisle coercion, 1932 home classroom, 1934 repaired building and 1978 school.

sources.title: Chitimacha Tribe: Language
sources.note: Direct tribal language history: Benjamin Paul, Delphine Decloux Stouff, Swadesh records and school revitalization. No exact recorded-hours total repeated.

sources.title: Daniel W. Hieber: Chitimacha, grammatical chapter
sources.note: Direct author-uploaded full chapter, printed page 1506 example 1: we haksigam hix siksi his nuytiqi / the young man answered the eagle. Page 1505 footnote 6 identifies A as Benjamin Paul. Page 1504 practical orthography. Extracted numerical citation glyphs partly garbled, sentence and English readable; does not claim rendered visual inspection.

sources.title: Chitimacha Tribe: RiverCane elder program
sources.note: Full indexed official program description, independent housing, meals, home delivery, health checks, activities and transport. Exact query site:chitimacha.gov/departments-services/rivercane meals pressure glucose. No changing fees, employee names or participation totals repeated.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Single historical Tunica record, with later Tunica-Biloxi continuity explained. First world_1492 polygon bbox [-92.5263,31.9360,-90.2727,33.5535], lower Mississippi; subsequent migrations are not implied by the static outline. Preserve imported 1492 to 1783 dates. Do not attach separate Biloxi, Ofo, Avoyel or Choctaw records; successor membership does not collapse earlier identities.

Proposed same-people association, not an association with distinct modern Biloxi-Chitimacha communities. First chitimacha world_1492 MultiPolygon bbox [-92.2347,29.0577,-89.0451,30.3130]; first chtimacha world_1530 Polygon bbox [-92.0187,29.0575,-89.0307,30.2327]. Both overlap the southern Louisiana homeland named by the Tribe, with near-identical labels; chronological gap is imported map coverage, not creation of a new people. Public opening states both phase dates. Preserve chitimacha 1492 to 1500 and chtimacha 1530 to 1783; later displacement, Charenton community and living Tribe covered. No Washa/Chawasha or Biloxi-Chitimacha IDs absorbed.
